notes: CLASS SWEEP 4 of 4, 2026-07-30 (+1 test, 1472 -> 1473; +1 file, 196 -> 197). The last unexamined surface: does a context().value gate actually cover what its handler spends? The class is PROVEN four times in this session — gate 14124 understated by ~2,600,000 so the 100M mint failed in ACTION behind a green COMPUTE; gate 14714 simply omitted ATH_TRANSFER_NOTIFY_STORAGE_ENDOWMENT; gate 18015 was 56,602 short of measurement; ATHVesting pinned its downstream budget to a literal. All four are the same shape: a term the handler pays, absent from the sum the gate demands. Measuring 63 gates end to end is not affordable; matching their SHAPE is. VGATE-01 collects, per receiver, what the gate reaches (expanding local lets, file-level Int consts and single-expression funs, and stripping the self. prefix the gate writes them with) against what its outgoing legs actually send. RESULT: NO NEW DEFECTS. The sweep went 18 hits -> 9 -> 3 -> 0, and every step down was a gap in the SCAN rather than a clean contract — locals derived from the inbound value, gates expressed through a helper declared before them, constants reached only through a fun, and self.-prefixed tokens. Three legs remain listed as balance-funded with their reasons: two dead-man sweeps that move the contract own money by definition, and DepositCapsuleFee, whose leg IS covered but by a differently-named constant — left explicit rather than silenced, because a sum that covers a term it does not NAME is exactly the coupling that rots unnoticed. Mutation-verified by dropping RS_PROTOCOL_FEE from the sum RS_MIN_VALUE builds: RecordShard.CapsulePublish surfaces by name.

CEREMONY AUDIT part 3, 2026-07-30 (+2 tests, 1470 -> 1472; +1 file, 195 -> 196). Two remaining surfaces, both clean, and both now guarded rather than merely believed. SIGNER ROLES: all 21 control steps checked against the gate each receiver actually enforces. requireGenesisController and requireController map to genesis_controller_one_shot, requireTreasury to ton_treasury_receiver — including the counter-intuitive five (FeeAccumulator binds are signed by the TREASURY, not the controller; the controller would be refused). No mismatch. Also checked and clean: UsernameRegistry SealGenesis does NOT clear genesis_controller_address, so the 56-part art upload and SealArt work before or after it, and the ordering the art script documents is stricter than the contract requires rather than load-bearing. SIGNED BODIES: an operator sees a hash in Tonkeeper, not a meaning, so CEREMONY-BODY-01 decodes every signed body and compares its opcode against the one the named contract declares. This session moved two opcodes already (DeployTreasurySupply off the 0x41544807 collision, and the new ATHMaster top-up), so drift between a contract and a stale packet is a live failure mode, not a hypothetical. Mutation-verified by moving BindShardCode opcode without regenerating the packet — B13 surfaces by name. CEREMONY-BODY-02 additionally checks the declared cell_hash_hex is the hash of the body actually carried, because that comparison is the ONLY thing standing between a correct packet and a substituted body, and it proves nothing if the two fields in the file disagree with each other.

CEREMONY AUDIT part 2, 2026-07-30 (+3 tests, 1467 -> 1470; +1 file, 194 -> 195). THE FINDING: FeeAccumulator has FIVE one-shot genesis binds and NOTHING could check they landed. Every other contract in the ceremony has a seal that refuses while a bind is missing — that is the checkpoint. This contract has no seal at all, the genesis verifier does not snapshot the fields, and get_state() did not report them, so a skipped bind was silent at ceremony time. It is also permanent: 15051/15052/15053/15057/15059 each demand `== null` so it can never be re-bound, and the contract cannot be replaced because its address is baked into four immutable contracts. The failure surfaces much later as gate 15055 refusing a lane capsule fee or 15060 refusing every TicketRedeem, with that lane airdrop dead for good. The five flags are now exposed on the view (APPENDED, never inserted) and FAACC-BIND-01 measures the PARTIAL state — three bound, two skipped — because that is the state nobody could previously see. SUPPORTING: CEREMONY-ORDER-01 derives each seal preconditions from the CONTRACTS (which Bind sets which flag, which Seal demands it) and checks the packet lists them in a signable order. It passes — the order was correct — but not one of those constraints had been written down. CEREMONY-ORDER-02 then found the ergonomic hazard behind the finding: both BuybackBurn (B01, B02, B12) and FeeAccumulator (B09, B13..B16) have their binds SPLIT across the file, so an operator working contract-by-contract rather than line-by-line skips one. Every seal and both split groups now carry an order_note naming their prerequisites and gates. The FeeAccumulator view change moved its code, so the cascade ran again: FEE_SINK rebaked to EQAsK2s3Dv0Gr1tj8Ycznk_75eCWTy7paF3yFhgpL1dzGdLH and every derived artefact regenerated.

CEREMONY AUDIT, 2026-07-30 (+3 tests, 1464 -> 1467; +1 file, 193 -> 194). The ceremony had been EDITED five times this session and never read as a whole: 36 steps, several of them one-shot, where a wrong order bricks a contract permanently. FIRST FINDING is in a step I added myself hours earlier. W01..W04 endow the four protocol-owned official ATHWallets and carried must_be_signed_after: F02 — which is wrong for two of them and misleading for all four. Only W03 targets an account F02 creates and only W02 one F01 creates; W01 waits on the SEPARATE reserve-funding script and W04 on BuybackBurn first buyback, long after genesis. So two of these steps deliberately address accounts that DO NOT EXIST when they are signed, and nothing said so. That turns out to be safe, and it is now MEASURED instead of assumed: value parked on an uninitialised address survives the later deploy intact. The counter-measurement is what gives that meaning — the identical step signed against an EQ (bounceable) address returns the money and leaves the wallet on its four-and-a-half-year transfer float, with the ceremony reporting success either way. So the UQ target form is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic, and it held only because friendly() happens to emit UQ. CEREMONY-W-03 now pins it against the artefact an operator signs, mutation-verified by switching the emitter to the bounceable form. The misleading ordering note is replaced with what is actually true and why.

CLASS SWEEP 3 of 3, 2026-07-30 (+4 tests, 1460 -> 1464; +1 file, 192 -> 193). The tier-4/5 classification — these contracts do NOT force a full redeploy — rested entirely on three hooks having been WRITTEN. None had ever been exercised as a migration. The receiving half lives in clean-18 and does not exist, so what is testable today is the property the design actually depends on: can a successor AUTHENTICATE the message from what it carries plus the clean-17 code cell, the same derive-and-compare FeeAccumulator gate 15055 already performs. ANSWER: yes, for all three, and now measured. A ticket export carries (credits_k, owner) and the sender address rebuilds exactly from (clean-17 ticket code, owner) — a stranger claiming the same owner rebuilds elsewhere, so the check has teeth. A username proof carries (name_hash, live owner) and rebuilds from (item code, old registry, name_hash), which means a clean-18 registry derives PAST its predecessor rather than trusting it. The KeyShard proof carries the key material itself — enc/sign/scan/pq — not a pointer, so a successor adopts a usable identity rather than a dangling reference. TWO THINGS THE SWEEP MADE HONEST. First, the export cannot be driven to completion today at all: with no clean-18 receiver the message bounces and bounced<TicketCreditsMigrated> restores the credits exactly once — which is the correct behaviour and is now pinned rather than assumed. Second, MIG-01B measures the residual instead of describing it: exporting to any contract that SWALLOWS unknown bodies destroys the credits with no bounce to catch it. Gate 27035 closes only the self-export case; AirdropTicket own receive(_: Slice) {} makes every other clean-17 ticket a silent sink. No on-chain fix exists — the ticket cannot enumerate addresses it does not know — so the cost of one wrong address in a migration tool is now a measured number rather than a sentence in a comment.

CLASS SWEEP 2 of 3, 2026-07-30 (+3 tests, 1457 -> 1460; +1 file, 191 -> 192). Client copies of contract-side numbers. Caught three times in one week before this — RS_MIN_VALUE, PUBLIC_AVATAR_PUBLISH_VALUE, FA_BUYBACK — each time by accident and each time fixed as an instance. FOUND, and it is a different shape than the three: web/pwa-contract-transactions.mjs still exported three constants described entirely in terms of the VAULT, a contract clean-17 deleted. They were not dead prose — app.js fed two of them to the fee ESTIMATORS while the live direct-pay send paths attached completely different values. A user was shown 0.617 GRAM for a username mint and then handed a 1,100,000,000 signing request (78% understated), and 0.115 against 0.2 for a profile avatar (74%). No funds are lost to that; it is the number a person reads on the screen where they decide whether to trust the app, and it had been wrong since the Vault was removed. The third constant, PROFILE_AVATAR_NOTIFY_VALUE_NANOTONS, was referenced nowhere at all. Both registry-charge constants were also imported by tests/pwa-contract-transactions.test.ts without a single assertion on them, so the suite carried them without checking them. FIXED by making the send path and the estimator read ONE exported constant each, in the module that owns it. PVSEND-01/02 pin the estimator to the value actually signed; PVSEND-03 fails on any live client constant that still names the deleted Vault, so the class cannot come back through a new copy. Mutation-verified by re-pointing the estimator at the old 617,000,000 literal.

CLASS SWEEP 1 of 3, 2026-07-30 (+2 tests, 1455 -> 1457; +1 file, 190 -> 191). Prompted by the tier-3 result: the caller-funded-substitution defect was found in MarketStabilitySeller, fixed there, and then found AGAIN in FeeAccumulator days later — the same shape in a contract the same audit had already covered, because the fix went to the instance and never swept the tree. Closing instances does not close a class. SWEPT: all 27 permissionless receivers that send value, read rather than assumed. Result — 3 already fixed (MarketStabilitySeller, FeeAccumulator x2); 1 present but harmless (BuybackBurn.ExecuteBuybackChunk: a caller CAN cover the 51.05 GRAM envelope, but their money executes a real buyback and the contract own envelope reaches the treasury through the dead-man sweep, so the honest description is a donation, not an attack); the remaining 23 are structurally immune for reasons now written down — the four ATH-due flushes decrement against an IN-FLIGHT RECORD so the caller TON cannot stand in for it, the three proof lanes are bounded on BOTH sides and pay for the caller own request, the three shard retires pay the caller by design and are time-gated with the account destroyed, and the sweeps have genesis-bound destinations behind dead-man clocks. ALSO CONFIRMED while sweeping: both registries protect flush replay over their SELF-CLEARING pending maps rather than a permanent used-id set — the tombstone lesson that cost ATHWallet its ~21,845 ceiling, applied correctly here. THE GUARD IS THE POINT. PVS-01 enumerates permissionless value senders from the source and fails on any that is not in a reviewed list with its verdict, so a NEW one cannot ship until somebody writes down why it is safe; PVS-02 fails on stale entries, because a list naming receivers that no longer exist looks thorough while covering nothing. Mutation-verified by removing a sender() check from ATHMaster.ATHBurnNotification — it surfaces by name.

TIER-3 AUDIT, 2026-07-30 (+1 test, 1454 -> 1455). FeeAccumulator: rent horizon already fine at 192 years, so the question was its accounting — its address is baked into four immutable contracts, so it can never be replaced and any defect in it is permanent. FOUND: FlushTreasuryDue carried the SAME 1:1 subsidy shape found in MarketStabilitySeller during wave-8 and fixed there — 15022 asked the caller for FEEACCUMULATOR_FLUSH_EXEC_RESERVE while 15023 allowed flushing exactly FEEACCUMULATOR_MIN_TREASURY_FLUSH_TON, the same 5,000,000, so the inbound covered the outbound one for one and the contract own nanotons never moved. Wave-8 looked at this contract and did not look at this lane. Less severe here than in MSS, and the difference is named rather than glossed: SweepUnaccounted reclassifies the stranded proceeds (held stays, accounted drops) and SplitAccumulated returns them to treasury_due, so it was recoverable permissionlessly by anyone who noticed. THE FIRST FIX WAS WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION and its own test caught it. Returning the WHOLE inbound made the contract pay its own gas out of the backing, ~66,667 a flush — the identical "shortfall paid silently out of the float" this file warns about elsewhere. FEE-BACKING-02 measures the balance delta and went red. The correct shape returns only what the caller sent ABOVE the execution reserve, keeping the reserve gate 15022 exists to collect; the buyback leg additionally keeps BUYBACK_ACCEPT_RESERVE_EXEC_RESERVE, which rides out with the envelope by design. ALSO VERIFIED: every credit to accumulated/treasury_due/buyback_due/storage_reserve is gated on the TON actually arriving; SweepUnaccounted excludes the caller own value (myBalance - context().value) and returns the change under nativeReserve, so it is idempotent and cannot convert callers gas into protocol revenue. FeeAccumulator code changed, so the cascade ran again: the four baked FEE_SINK constants rebaked to EQCWTfItKphGS0sLee8xhOKcCZ6Tcs0hnuaT6O6uJuPWf6ws, shard code, hashes, both ceremony packets, the genesis verify report, the three economics reports and both deploy-prep modes regenerated.

TIER-2 AUDIT, 2026-07-30 (+2 tests, 1452 -> 1454). Four findings, all of one class, and the class is the same one that produced the tier-1 finding: a permanent account whose funding was fixed by hand and tied to nothing. FIRST, MEASURING ALL SIX permanent contracts rather than the three already measured — which is itself the finding about my own guard: MarketStabilitySeller, 159 code cells, 10,523,844 of rent a year, funded for 48 YEARS while holding 60,000,000 ATH, selling on no clock at all, with no administrative command in existence after the seal; BuybackBurn, 215 cells, the largest contract here, funded for 35 YEARS. Raised to 1.2 and 1.6 GRAM, and RENT-HORIZON-01 widened from three names to all six with the reason each is never-redeployable spelled out. SECOND, and larger: the ATH does not live in those contracts, it lives in their official ATHWallets, and those are separate accounts with their own rent. MSTAB-09 measures the real one end to end — after the genesis funding transfer, the wallet holding 60% of supply is left with 24,832,861 nanoton, FOUR AND A HALF YEARS at the measured 5,456,808 a year. Overpaying the transfer cannot fix it: everything above ATH_TRANSFER_NOTIFY_STORAGE_ENDOWMENT is refunded to the sender, and raising that constant is not an option because it is what EVERY user transfer carries. So the ceremony now carries W01..W04 — permissionless ATHWalletTopUpStorageReserve to each of the four wallets that receive once and thereafter only send — at 600,000,000 each, pinned by RENT-HORIZON-03. The two registry wallets are deliberately excluded: ordinary purchase traffic tops them up. ACCOUNTING VERIFIED across all three remaining tier-2 contracts: no bucket in AirdropPool, ATHVesting or BuybackBurn can be credited without matching TON or ATH actually arriving. MSS holds reserve + sold == funded across funding, finalisation and rollback. BuybackBurn RecycleRouteRefundReserve moves an envelope between buckets plus the caller top-up rather than creating one. ALSO CORRECTED: a MarketStabilitySeller comment claimed the buy path is "gated on pricing_frozen, :388". No such gate and no such field exist — the price became a compile-time constant. On a contract that can never be redeployed a stale line is read as the specification years later.

TIER-1 SECOND PASS, 2026-07-30 (+2 tests, 1450 -> 1452; +1 file, 189 -> 190). The first pass checked four AXES and was reported as if it had checked the CONTRACT; the owner pushed back and was right. This pass walks all 30 entry points of ATHWallet and all of ATHMaster, handler by handler. NEWLY READ AND FOUND CORRECT: PruneStaleNotification deletes an escrow entry WITHOUT refunding — which is right, not a loss: the ATH is credited to the recipient on ARRIVAL, so the escrow is over the refund RIGHT, not over the money, and letting it lapse is the recipient keeping a payment exactly as TEP-74 has no escrow at all. The lane discriminator is clean: response_ack_value 1,000,000 => 24h TTL for the plain lane, 3,000,000 => 7 days for both registry lanes, and both registries hold 86,400 TTLs, so the refunding side always moves first with six days of margin. refund_pending_notification debits, deletes the key, and re-stores an outgoing pending entry, so a refund is exactly-once. All five outgoing bounces route to one restore that keys on sender(), matches the stored amount and deletes the key. JettonTransfer is owner-only, stores its pending entry BEFORE debiting. There is no external() receiver at all, so no gas-credit surface exists on the token cluster. A MIS-STATEMENT CORRECTED MID-PASS: I first read the bounce budget as 32+64+160=256 over a 224 limit and called the notification lane broken. Wrong — the 32-bit opcode is INSIDE the 256-bit slice, so fields get exactly 224 and query_id(64)+sender_key(160)=224 fits precisely. No defect. But the margin is ZERO, and the internal-transfer lane has only 32 bits spare, while the failure mode is a parser underflow that consumes the only refund trigger and loses the ATH with no trace. AirdropTicket and FeeAccumulator carry this rule in comments; ATHWallet did not. BOUNCE-PREFIX-01 now derives the readable prefix of every bounced type in the whole contracts tree from its declaration and fails if it passes 224 — mutation-verified by widening sender_key to uint192.

TIER-1 TARGETED AUDIT, 2026-07-30 (+3 tests, 1447 -> 1450; +1 file, 188 -> 189). Scope chosen deliberately narrow: the two contracts a defect in which cannot be repaired by ANY migration, because redeploying them changes the token itself — ATHWallet (its code IS the jetton wallet, embedded in six other contracts) and ATHMaster. AXES VERIFIED, not read: supply conservation — all six balance credits are gated on sender() == derive_wallet_address(claimed owner), so a credit is impossible without a matching debit at a real wallet running this exact bytecode; every one of the five outgoing debits plus the burn is bounce:true with a matching bounced handler that restores; the burn is owner-only (14000) and the master decrements supply only on a message from the derived wallet of the named owner; supply can never increase after genesis (14121 is one-shot and a forged bounce cannot reopen it — already pinned by an existing test). ONE FINDING, and it is real: ATHMaster was funded for 77 years against its own 100-year commitment. MEASURED 97 distinct code cells => 6,496,200 of rent a year at the frozen rate, against a flat 500,000,000 deploy value. Past that point the jetton master goes into storage debt: burns stop being recorded and get_jetton_data stops answering, so every explorer, wallet and DEX loses the token identity — on the one contract that can never be redeployed. Raised to 1,000,000,000 (~154 years) and, more importantly, tied to the code by RENT-HORIZON-01/02, which DERIVE the requirement from the compiled BOC. This class had already bitten ATHVesting the day before at ~67 years, and both times the number was a hand-written literal with nothing connecting it to the code whose rent it pays. ALSO MEASURED, and closed as bounded rather than fixed: neither ATHWallet map has a cap. An unsettled escrow entry costs 2.98 cells, so ~22,028 of them reach the ~65,536-cell account ceiling; a stranger can open them for one atomic unit of ATH plus 45,000,000 of TON each. ATHTOMB-03 measures it and pins the property that matters — the owner can still spend their own ATH with a backlog in place. Recovery is cheap and permissionless: pruning a single stale entry SHRINKS the state and restores writes, so the worst case is a temporary, self-healing grief costing the attacker ~990 GRAM and the defender ~0.002.

WAVE-8 FINDING #17 CLOSED, 2026-07-30 (+2 tests, 1445 -> 1447) — the last of the 53. PublicShard get_page did not return the publisher, and the omission was argued from the wrong threat: forging a body to a stored commit is a sha256 preimage, but an attacker does not forge one, they REPUBLISH someone else's byte for byte. Gate 13702 binds no sender for BEACON or THREAD, so the duplicate is accepted and creates a second entry with the same body_commit. TWO halves were needed and each is mutation-verified to be load-bearing on its own: the row now carries the low 128 bits of the authoritative publisher's account hash (320 -> 448 bits, 3 -> 2 rows per cell) so the client VERIFIES instead of inferring, AND on a duplicate commit the OLDEST entry_id wins instead of the last — the tag alone does not help, because both entries are genuine and each matches its own publisher. SECOND-ORDER, closed by measurement not by rounding the rule down: the extra code grew the account, so the AVATAR shard (the longest-lived kind) fell to a 1.4956x rent margin against the project 1.5x rule. PS_BASE_ENDOWMENT_AVATAR 21.5M -> 21.8M, which moved deploy_min_value, which moved the CLIENT figure PUBLIC_AVATAR_PUBLISH_VALUE 39.2M -> 39.5M — leaving that behind would have had gate 13704 refuse every first avatar publish in production with every contract test green. PS-TAG-01 now pins the contract and client row widths to each other, because a width mismatch is silent on both sides: it produces an empty or garbled feed, never an error.

WAVE-8 PRE-SEAL AUDIT CLOSED + CASCADE, 2026-07-30 (+47 tests, 1398 -> 1445; +8 files, 180 -> 188). 53 findings dispositioned across six batches: 46 fixed, 2 disproven by measurement (#32 the TicketRedeem 2,000,000 reserve — the balance does NOT fall on a redeem; #50 shard-squat storage debt — MEASURED at four ages up to 40 years and a debt 2.5x the whole publish value, the publish is still admitted, does not abort and stores its record), 4 already closed by an earlier batch, 1 deferred (#17 PublicShard get_page does not return the publisher, so a channel can be taken over in the catalogue by republishing a body byte for byte — the fix is a wire-format change spanning the contract, the client decoder and the catalogue sweep, and it was deliberately NOT landed on a red-from-cascade public-lane suite that could not tell it from the cascade). Genesis-critical: ATHMaster minted the 100,000,000 ATH by paying for itself out of a balance nobody had tied to the gate — MEASURED 754,268 gas + 3,826,734 of action-phase forward fees against a 2,000,000 reserve, and the failure mode was rc37 in ACTION with COMPUTE exiting 0, invisible to every exit-code check. The suite PINNED that defect as a property in GENESIS-ACTION-01..03; those three tests plus one more now assert its inverse. The treasury ATH wallet that holds 100% of supply was left with 1,624,999 against a MEASURED 5,132,011/year of rent — the surplus is now forwarded to it and D02 raised 5M -> 620M for a century. AirdropPool genesis seal was permanently DoS-able by one extra atomic unit from any stranger. A stale ACK could close a paid username purchase for 4,000,000 nanoton with no NFT and no refund, and one ordinary NFT transfer made an unfinished mint unrecoverable forever. One stray UploadArt key made SealArt impossible for good. The stuck-PENDING class (7 contracts waiting on a terminal from the ATHWallet lane, including the whole 60,000,000 ATH MSS reserve) was fixed ONCE, in the wallet, without guessing: the pending_outgoing record is deleted by the recipient ack, so its presence after the grace PROVES the transfer never landed. CASCADE: FeeAccumulator and ATHWallet code moved, so all 16 contracts were rebuilt, the four baked FEE_SINK constants rebaked to EQBHysiwpmRtWQlwfkiHnlZqgOVqv4t-PoojAfzQRJVEZ5rE, web/shard-code.mjs regenerated, ceremony packets and the three economics reports regenerated, and the ATH-master / M20F / BuybackBurn-checklist pins rebaselined. FA_BUYBACK turned out to be a copy of a DERIVED address duplicated across seven test files, and the sink address a literal in four more; both are now single-sourced in tests/helpers/fee-sink-fixture.ts and tied to the ceremony draft by FA-SOURCE-01/02.

ATHWallet pending_outgoing ratchet fixed 2026-07-29 (+2 tests, 1396 -> 1398; +1 file, 179 -> 180). ATH_INTERNAL_TRANSFER_SOURCE_ACK_VALUE raised 1M -> 4M. It funds the ONLY path that clears pending_outgoing_transfers, a map with no bound, no prune, no getter and — until tests/ath-wallet-pending-outgoing-ratchet.test.ts — no test at all. ATHWallet never calls accept_message, so the message value IS the gas budget: 1M bought exactly 15,000 units at 66.667/unit, while clearing costs a hash plus a dict get and delete whose price grows with tree DEPTH. Measured in the sandbox, worst of 24 sampled keys per size: N=1 -> 6,499 gas; N=2000 -> 14,724 (276 spare); N=4000 -> 14,999 and exit -14 on 2 of 24; N=6000 -> 6 of 24; N=9000 -> 10 of 24. Past ~4,000 entries the ack silently ran out of gas — sent bounce:false, so no party learned anything, the entry became permanent, and sending kept working on a budget 48x larger: a one-way ratchet toward the account cell ceiling on an immutable contract. Reachability was NOT demonstrated (entries clear on both ack and bounce, and every transfer carries initOf ATHWallet so the recipient is always a real wallet), but the margin was 1.8% with no way to even observe the map from outside. CASCADE, because ATHWallet code is embedded wherever an ATH wallet address is derived: all 16 contracts rebuilt, FeeAccumulator moved, the four baked FEE_SINK constants rebaked, web/shard-code.mjs and every ceremony artifact regenerated, and the ATH-master / M20F / BuybackBurn-checklist pins rebaselined. The wave-7 ceremony guard earned itself here: it refused to emit a packet on the real, unplanned mismatch, naming all four contracts — not in a mutation test but in anger. Two behavioural mirrors moved with gate 14314 (74M -> 77M) rather than being papered over, and the coupled 45M notify floor was re-checked against the new 29M arrival gate (~1.33x, was ~1.47x) instead of assumed.

Wave-8 final independent contract audit, 2026-07-28/29 (+6 tests, 1390 -> 1396). Independent by construction: the finder agents were deliberately NOT given the previous waves findings, because that list would have told them where not to look. Coverage is provable rather than claimed — each of the 16 slices had to return one record per handler, and 168 records came back against 167 handlers enumerated from source. MEASURED BY HAND, not relayed: (a) all 16 production contracts rebuild byte-for-byte from source, so the audited .tact is exactly what deploys; (b) 18 of 20 mirrored message declarations are byte-identical and the two that differ do so on purpose (RetireShard is per-lane so a retire aimed at the wrong shard type is refused); (c) every opcode literal the client writes resolves to a real contract message, and the one orphan is the IS_BODY_DOMAIN constant, which matches IntroShard.tact:60. NEW GUARDS: shard-code-hash-evidence extended from 3 contracts to all 16, plus EVID-05, which compares the committed code-hash evidence against build/ rather than against another artifact — the check deferred for the whole clean-17 branch as permanently red, now meaningful because the seal rebaseline made the artifact current. GENESIS-ACTION-01..03 pin a measured defect in the ceremony first step: DeployTreasurySupply gate 14124 checks the message value, but the binding constraint is ATHMasters OWN balance, because the downstream send carries a full StateInit whose forward fee comes out of balance while the handler refunds everything the gate did not require. At 2,000,000 of own balance the ACTION phase fails rc37 and none of the 100M ATH is minted, while COMPUTE exits 0 so exit-code checks report success; sending more value does not help. Production is safe only because D01 funds the master with 500,000,000, a number tied to this requirement by nothing until H-DEP-DRYRUN-09.

Ceremony STEP ORDER seal gate audited 2026-07-28 (+2 tests, 1388 -> 1390). The runbook — the document a human follows on ceremony day — still told the operator to deploy and seal `Vault` and `CapsuleHub`, contracts deleted in clean-17, and to fund `vault_official_ath_wallet`; 17 stale mentions in all. The ceremony SCRIPTS were already clean-17, so nothing went red: only the prose had drifted. Worse, the guard meant to protect this ordering (SPEC-MSG-SOURCE-03E) was itself pinned to `Vault.SealGenesis`/`CapsuleHub.SealGenesis` — a guard aimed at a deleted contract is not a weak guard, it is an absent one. Runbook rebaselined onto AirdropPool; guard rebaselined and extended to refuse the deleted names outright. New H-DEP-DRYRUN-07/08 pin the packet's own execution_order (binds -> funding -> off-chain verify -> seal) and require the runbook's seal list to equal the packet's, naming only contracts that still have sources. Measured while auditing: the order is enforced ON CHAIN at both edges of the funding step (AirdropPool 26011/26019 refuse a deposit notification before ath_master is bound; 26044 refuses the seal until funded_amount == 15M), so a wrong order fails loudly rather than silently.

The correct design: a SHARE is an internal REFERENCE — the block already carries entryId + bodyHash, and the original public post's image ALREADY lives on-chain, retained >=1 YEAR (CapsuleHub CAPSULEHUB_INDEX_RETENTION_SECONDS = 31536000; the publish-path FIFO deletes oldest-first ONLY past that window, so nothing younger than a year is ever evicted), readable by anyone via provider.getPublicEntry(entryId) (subscription-free public data — I had wrongly claimed non-subscribers couldn't read it). So re-uploading a thumbnail was rejected as duplication. IMPLEMENTATION: buildSharedPostEmbed, when block.hasImage, calls resolveSharedPostImageUrl(block.entryId, block.bodyHash): findCachedPublicPostByEntryId scans the feed cache (eachCachedPublicPost) for a post whose entryId/readEntryId matches, warms its stripped image from the durable per-post media store (publicPostMediaStore, keyed by post.id) via applyPublicPostMediaRecord, and returns the image data-url; the .then swaps the text media-hint for a real (img.src = a decoded data-url, never innerHTML = XSS-safe). A cold recipient (channel not cached) keeps the hint, and the embed header still taps through to the live original channel. REFERENCE INTEGRITY (adversarial-review finding, LOW, FIXED): resolveSharedPostImageUrl verifies the resolved post's bodyHash == the SHARE block's bodyHash (normalizeBodyHashHex, content-addressed) before showing the image — else a crafted entryId (the whole SHARE block is sender-authored) could show an UNRELATED cached post's image under a spoofed channel/label. Only the recipient's OWN decoded media is ever shown; sender bytes never cross the wire. Adversarial review: 1 finding (the spoof, low) -> fixed with the bodyHash check; all other axes clean (throws try/catch-wrapped, no cache corruption, isConnected guard blocks a stale/wrong-embed swap, the feedPostClampObserver still tracks the added image). RULE: the visual-viewport keyboard-detection baseline MUST be keyed to the viewport WIDTH (or reset on orientation change) — a plain monotonic-max baseline reads 'keyboard open' forever in the shorter orientation. RULE: the only reliable way to stop a focused editable from re-showing the soft keyboard on a geometry change is to BLUR it; gate that blur on a device-capability query ((pointer: coarse)), never on a viewport-shrink latch (which desktop resize/zoom/DevTools trips). v723 identity-bleed THE ACTUAL ONGOING ROOT — receive-side sender resolves to own (owner on-device diagnostic, 2026-07-08): the v722 heal cleaned the thread variants (diagnostic confirmed Saved carried ONLY the own wallet, peer thread ONLY the peer), yet peer replies STILL landed in 'My notes' and were marked 'received'. Root proven from the diagnostic: threadForChainCapsule resolves the sender via resolvePrivateCapsuleSenderWallet = resolveKnownPrivateSenderWallet(opened) ?? privateEntryPublisherWallet(entry). When the CRYPTOGRAPHIC resolveKnown fails (flaky RPC on the recipient's TMA), it falls back to the chain entry publisher — which on the RECIPIENT index is the OWN wallet — so senderWallet===own, privateWalletIdentityVariants(own) matches the Saved thread by its own-wallet variant, and the peer message files into 'My notes' with NO variant graft. The meta stays 'received' because that path uses isSelfOpenedCapsule(opened) (reads the decrypted payload.senderWallet=peer), which disagreed with the routing. This fires regardless of any variant cleanup, which is why v719-v722 never fixed it. FIX (adversarially reviewed, 3-lens): (1) privateEntryPublisherWallet returns null when author_wallet===own (never the sender of a received message). (2) threadForChainCapsule: a SELF capsule (isSelfOpenedCapsule) pins senderWallet=own so self-notes always route to Saved even when key resolution fails; a NON-self capsule whose resolved sender is own is set to NULL (-> inbound peer thread keyed by senderKeyId, pendingIdentityResolution, re-bound on recovery) — NEVER own. v721 STALE-BUILD DELIVERY fix (owner repro persisted after v720, 2026-07-08): the receiving TMA profile still showed peer replies inside 'My notes' minutes after the v720 deploy — and this time the ROOT was PROVEN, not guessed: (1) curl -sI https://platho.app/ shows the server sends NO Cache-Control on the app shell (only ETag/Last-Modified), and (2) sw.js navigationResponse did a plain fetch(event.request), which is answered by the browser HTTP cache FIRST — so webviews (worst: the Telegram Mini App, Chromium heuristic caching = 10% of time-since-Last-Modified) served a STALE index.html (old ?v= asset URLs) for hours without ever asking the network. 'Network-first' was defeated by the HTTP-cache layer UNDER fetch(); devices kept running old builds no matter how many times the user 'updated'. FIX: the shell navigation fetch is rebuilt as new Request(url, {cache:'no-cache', credentials:'same-origin'}) — forces conditional revalidation (ETag -> cheap 304 or fresh 200). The fixed sw.js reaches even stale devices via the browser's SW-update channel (the SW main script is fetched bypassing the HTTP cache per spec). ALSO: the heal math of v719/v720 was validated empirically in node against the real modules (createRecipientThread(own).id IS in the heal's savedIds set; friendly/raw identityKey forms both covered by the drop sets) — the heals are sound, the failing device simply never ran them. ALSO: build badge duplicated onto the Profile pane (#profileVersionLabel, setText from PLATHO_APP_RUNTIME_VERSION) — the rail badge is invisible on the narrow mobile/TMA layout, so there was NO on-device way to verify a TMA build. PWA-CONFIG-08 pins the no-cache shell fetch; PWA-CONFIG-08B nav pin updated (fetchWithTimeout(shellRequest,...)); PWA-CONFIG-01B pins the Profile badge mirror. RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP (server, admin-SSH — owner decision): add Cache-Control headers at Caddy (no-cache for / + /index.html + /sw.js; long immutable for ?v= assets) to close the FIRST-visit / SW-less hole too. v719 CRITICAL cross-wallet identity-bleed fix (owner repro, 2026-07-08): a FRESH account (new iPhone wallet W_A) that added the contact glasnost (owned by a DIFFERENT wallet W_B, verified on-chain: registry get_name_record -> 0:741122e8...dd4b1157) saw the W_B private dialog render as its OWN 'My notes' Saved thread, the conversation with a second contact ALSO landed in 'My notes', and the user's own public channel 'You' wore glasnost's avatar. ROOT (3-agent trace + 4-lens adversarial review, both Workflow): (1) the private composer submit fell back to threads[0] — ALWAYS the Saved self-thread — when activeThreadId was unresolved, double-homing the outgoing echo in Saved; (2) when the chain scan later reopened that sent capsule and routed it to the real W_B thread, relocateExistingCapsuleMessage's duplicate-dialog merge grafted the emptied Saved thread's ENTIRE variant set — including the OWN wallet_address variant — onto the W_B thread; from then isSavedMessagesThread(W_B thread) === true (renders as 'My notes') and publicAvatarUrlForWallet(W_A)'s thread fallback resolves the W_B thread's avatar onto the own channel. Wire routing/encryption was ALWAYS correct (messages encrypted to the true recipient key) — display/identity-association only. FIX (7 guards): (A) activeThread() + composer submit + the 'selected thread vanished' rebuild branch + pruneEmptyAnonymousPeerThreads NEVER fall back to threads[0]/Saved (null -> list/empty state, composer gating consistent via canEditPrivateComposerDraft(null)=false); (B) relocateExistingCapsuleMessage never consumes the Saved thread as a merge source and carries ONLY non-wallet (username/DNS) variants into the survivor; (C) resolveWalletChannelDisplay's own-wallet branch returns UNCONDITIONALLY (own linked .ath or null — never falls through to the contact store / private-thread fallback); (D) writeContactDisplayPreference refuses + clears any entry keyed by the own wallet; (G) hydrateThreadDisplayFromContactStore short-circuits for the own wallet; (F) healCrossWalletIdentityBleed() one-time self-heal on every history restore for devices poisoned BEFORE the fix (the grafted variants persist in encrypted-history thread snapshots and applyHistoryThreadSnapshot re-adds them additively): own-wallet variant may live ONLY on the real Saved thread (identified by its CREATION id, not the poisoned variants), Saved carries NOTHING but the own wallet, affected snapshots rewritten via persistThreadDisplayPreference + own-wallet contact-display entry cleared; (E, defense-in-depth) publicPostAuthorIdentityButton click re-checks isOwnPublicAuthor. Adversarial review verdicts: merge SOUND, display SOUND, send REGRESSION_RISK resolved by aligning activeThread() with the submit (single source of truth), completeness INCOMPLETE resolved by F+G. RELATED spawned task: prefs-snapshot divert accepts foreign-authored prefs blocks (subscription/username injection) — separate fix via entry.author_wallet, NOT isSelfOpenedCapsule (anonymous sender mode omits senderWallet -> would break cross-device restore). +1 test PWA-IDENTITY-BLEED-01 (pins all guards + the heal). 2026-07-06 PWA v693 HOTFIX for two runtime bugs that v692 shipped and the GREP-ONLY test suite could not catch (it readFileSync's app.js, never EXECUTES it). Found via owner on-device screenshots + a real browser boot. (1) BOOT CRASH (TDZ): `let publicFeedShownCap = PUBLIC_FEED_RENDER_CAP` sat ABOVE the `const PUBLIC_FEED_RENDER_CAP` declaration, so that module-load statement forward-referenced the const in its temporal dead zone -> 'Cannot access PUBLIC_FEED_RENDER_CAP before initialization' at module load -> boot-guard error screen, app dead. Fix: declare `let publicFeedShownCap;` with the other public state, INITIALIZE it just after the const is declared. (2) F2-virt FEED DUPLICATION: renderPublicFeed's keyed reconciliation REBUILT an <article> when its render signature changed (e.g. avatar hydrates between the frequent re-renders) but did not remove the OLD node -- the final cleanup only removes ids NOT in `seen`, and the rebuilt node re-claims the same id, so the stale node lingered; each signature-changing render leaked another card (owner saw 4 identical 'Waiting for public feed' PLATHO cards). Fix: on a signature change REMOVE the stale node before rebuilding, and dedupe the `existing` map (keep first node per id, drop duplicates) so a polluted DOM self-heals. VERIFIED this time by a REAL clean browser boot of the fixed app.js (no boot-guard, exactly one platho card, zero duplicates) AND an extraction test driving 3 signature-changing re-renders + a 4-duplicate pre-seed (both collapse to 1). LESSON: grep-tests cannot catch module-load-order or render-dedup bugs -- app.js changes need a real page boot + a signature-CHANGE render path, not isolated function calls with stable inputs. Version app v692->693, SW cache v763->764; deploy-prep regenerated.

2026-06-23 PWA v487 -- fix the keyless 429 backoff bug (Part 1 of the RPC-pacing rewrite; see plan + [[unified-rpc-request-pump]]). ROOT CAUSE of a keyless image taking ~10 min to send with only ~2 429s (multi-agent trace workflow wft77nkkb): toncenterHttpError (web/vault-ton-rpc-provider.mjs) HARDCODED retryAfterMs=TONCENTER_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF_MS=60000 on a 429 WITHOUT a Retry-After header, overriding the configured rateLimitBackoffMs=7000. The transport's own state.backoffUntil already used 7000 correctly; only the ERROR object's retryAfterMs was wrong, and it propagated up to the app-level limiter (tonRpcLimitedUntil -> 60s park) + the higher retry loops' reschedule (confirm/sync/send), so after each 429 the app slept a full minute issuing ZERO requests (~10-15 reqs over ~10 min instead of using the ~1rps budget). (2) app.js tonRpcLimitBackoffMs clamps a trusted error.retryAfterMs to the configured ceiling (honors a smaller server value; never lets a large/stale value re-introduce a multi-minute app park). Effect: the existing confirm/send/sync loops reschedule at ~7s not 60s -> keyless image send ~10 min -> ~1-2 min. NEW functional regression test VAULT-RPC-04C2 (a 429 with no Retry-After + rateLimitBackoffMs:7000 -> error.retryAfterMs===7000, proving no more hardcoded 60s). 2026-06-19 PWA v443 — FIX: a 2-capsule (64KB) PRIVATE image hung forever on 'submitted 2/2, confirming' and never reached the recipient, while the SAME image published fine as a profile AVATAR. ROOT (two independent adversarial investigations + an on-chain probe, didExecute=never): a 64KB image splits into two size_class-32 capsules that groupPublishItemsIntoBatches packed into ONE 2-part signed external; a private HYBRID body is padded to size_class*1024 + 1204 (ML-KEM768 ciphertext 1088 + prefix) and carries TWO header cells, so the two-part private external serialized to ~70KB — over TON's max_ext_msg_size (config-43 = 65535 bytes). TON validators DROP an oversized inbound external at ingest BEFORE the Vault external() receiver runs (no acceptMessage, no publish_nonce bump, no receipt, no bounce — see contracts/Vault.tact EXT_HARD_BITS=65535*8), so both parts pinned at PUBLISH_PART_STATUS_SENT, submittedCount/confirmedCount stayed 0 forever (displaySubmittedCount=2 is only the optimistic broadcast counter). The avatar of the same image is PUBLIC (variable-length unpadded body, ONE header) so it stayed under the ceiling. Single-capsule private works. The PWA packer had NO byte guard (groupPublishItemsIntoBatches split only on kind + MAX_BATCH_PARTS=8; buildBatchPublishExternalBoc serialized with no length check). FIX (PWA-side; the mainnet Vault is immutable and correct — it never saw the message): (1) web/publish-batch-orchestration.mjs groupPublishItemsIntoBatches now also starts a new batch when the estimated serialized external would exceed MAX_BATCH_EXTERNAL_BYTES=62000 (estimatePublishItemExternalBytes = size_class*1024 + (public?1200:4000)); large capsules ride ONE part per external (the proven-good single-part path), small capsules still amortize up to 8. (3) web/app.js schedulePrivatePublishConfirmationRetry + resumePendingPrivatePublishConfirmations: the stable-age terminal (privatePendingPublishConfirmAgeMs >= NO_PROGRESS_DEADLINE, anchored on messageCreatedAtMs, reset-proof) now fires for ANY not-fully-confirmed publish, not only confirmedCount===0, so a PARTIAL multi-external publish (one of two externals confirmed) reaches the durable red terminal instead of hanging (the per-resume scheduleImmediate attempt reset otherwise defeats the attempt>=ACTIVE_LIMIT*4 backstop for partials). Independently adversarially verified (4 lenses: double-spend / under-split / quote-send-consistency / partial-terminal): 0 real defects, verdict GO (high confidence; worst packer-producible external ~55574 B, largest single sc=32 capsule ~35618 B — both well under 65535, so the hard guard only fires on a forced non-packer shape). 2026-06-18 cross-session auto-retry for stuck private-receive entries (#9, designed + adversarially verified). PROBLEM: a private index entry that the per-session 3-strikes unknown-error skip buries (cursor advances past it; the in-memory strike Map dies on reload, so a reload starting from the advanced cursor never re-scans it) was permanently lost unless the user hit 'Sync messages'. FIX (all web/app.js, v434): a NEW persistent localStorage store ('platho.private.chain.stuck.entry.v1', keyed by hub+keyId, records {entryId, strikes, lastError, firstSeen/lastSeen}) mirroring the body-history-unavailable store. The 3-strikes ELSE now persists the skipped entry (rememberPrivateStuckEntry, returns the cross-session strike); its ids are UNIONed into the existing retryEntryIds replay set (re-scanned each session regardless of the advanced cursor); the record is cleared on genuine success (empty / open-ok, NOT before the open); after PRIVATE_SCAN_UNKNOWN_ERROR_CROSS_SESSION_CAP=8 cross-session strikes the entry is PROMOTED to a surfaced 'undelivered' gap (filtered out of the replay set so it is re-fetched 0 times thereafter) and surfaced via a new undeliveredCount (read from the STORE, not the per-run skipped counter, so it survives reload) wired into privateSyncResult + privateSyncStatusText ('N undelivered') + the completeMessageSyncUi gate + the reason ladder ('private_entry_undelivered'). THE LOAD-BEARING CORRECTION (both adversarial verdicts): the retryEntryIds replay loop does `if (!result.ok) break`, so a stuck id fed in must NOT return {ok:false} (would stall the whole pass + cursor every session — a worse loop than v419-v421). scanPrivateEntryId now has a fast-path: a persisted/replayed stuck entry (alreadyStuck = source==='history-retry' || hasPrivateStuckEntry) on re-fail bumps the persistent strike and returns {ok:true} immediately (one read, never scanComplete=false), mirroring body-history's non-blocking contract; only a FRESH index-walk unknown error keeps the per-session 3-strikes ramp. BOUNDED (no poison loop): the cursor write gate is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED (recovery is the replay set, not cursor manipulation); per-session replay is capped by AUTO_LIMIT=2 + the 3-min cooldown; lifetime re-fetches per entry <= CAP=8 then 0 (the strikes>=CAP filter sits BEFORE the cooldown so promoted ids never consume the auto budget). Manual 'Sync messages' (forceHistoryRetry/forceIndexRescan) uses the manual limit (16) for the stuck set too. Test PWA-RECEIVE-RETRY-01; PWA-CONFIG-07B retry-set assertions updated for the union + the ternary scan-log. app v433->v434, SW cache v504->v505; deploy-prep regenerated. This completes the send/receive reliability arc (v430 activation -> v431 burst-send/gateway -> v432 receive-gap -> v433 double-publish -> v434 cross-session retry). npm.cmd test = 114/114 test files, 1002/1002 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).

2026-06-18 double-publish / double-spend hardening (after an adversarially-verified multi-agent investigation that NARROWED the risk: the broad public-double and nonce-floor theories were REFUTED as reachable; exactly ONE live path remained). MECHANISM (#1, rare but irreversible): a private publish part broadcast at nonce N gets an AMBIGUOUS result (5xx/timeout) but ACTUALLY lands; ~150s later the receipt ring slot (nonce%20) is evicted so confirmVaultBatchReceiptsFromPublishState misses it; recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts then asks provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex, which in DEGRADED-verification survival mode (common on RU networks: keyless toncenter 403/429 → one unverified replica) read a lagging replica that had not yet indexed the landed entry → returned 'absent' → the part was cleared + reset to BUILT + fresh-re-signed at the now-advanced nonce N+1 → the SAME private entry published twice + double TON spend. FIVE fixes (all web/app.js): (1) provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex is now FAIL-CLOSED — it returns 'inconclusive' (never 'absent') when tonRpcVerificationStructurallyDegraded(), and forces verify:true/allowUnverifiedCriticalRead:false; so a fresh re-sign can only follow a VERIFIED absence proof. (2) before any clear+reset, recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts cross-checks the kind-agnostic receipt ring with a VERIFIED read — CONFIRMED→confirm (no re-sign), any non-EVICTED status (PROCESSING/REJECTED/BOUNCED)→no re-sign, only a missing/EVICTED receipt + verified 'absent' authorizes the re-sign; a failed verified receipt read also blocks it. (3) the ambiguous batch-publish catch now raises vaultPublishNonceFloor (cross-path consistency with the success path + single-external helpers). (4) the LATENT public-part hole is guarded by construction (provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex + recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts both skip non-private parts) — not reachable today (recover's only caller is the private confirm driver) but safe if public dropped-recovery is ever wired. (5) a non-'absent'/inconclusive consumed-nonce part is NEVER re-signed — it stays UNKNOWN, keeps idempotently re-broadcasting its one real external, and the existing 15-min partial-retry-deadline surfaces it as a manual-retry block (no silent loss, no auto-double-spend). TRADEOFF (owner-confirmed): in degraded verification a genuinely-dropped message can no longer auto-fresh-resign — it relies on idempotent same-nonce re-broadcast + manual retry; this trades a longer degraded-mode pending window for the absolute no-double-spend guarantee. Test PWA-DOUBLEPUBLISH-01 pins all four guards. app v432->v433, SW cache v503->v504; deploy-prep regenerated. PENDING follow-up: cross-session auto-retry for stuck receive entries (the precise/prompt blocked-state surfacing is the deferred refinement of #5). npm.cmd test = 114/114 test files, 1001/1001 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).

2026-06-18 private RECEIVE-delivery-gap fix (after an adversarially-verified multi-agent investigation of: sender shows all messages 'published' but a recipient that reports '✓ Synced' is permanently missing a non-contiguous subset, incl. an image). ROOT: receive-side truthfulness + permanent-drop — completeMessageSyncUi (web/app.js) reported 'synced' while per-entry skip paths dropped entries, and the cursor advanced past them (permanent across sessions). PRIMARY trigger: a transient RPC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE error ('TON RPC verification unavailable') was matched by isPrivateOpenKeyMismatchError's /unavailable/i and routed into the PERMANENT unreadable-capsule branch (reason private_key_open_failed + cursor advance) → dropped forever while the header said 'Synced'; each entry fails independently → the non-contiguous shape; the v430 recipient under a /messages 429 storm (the same storm v431 #5 fixed for the SENDER path) generated exactly these errors. THREE fixes (all web/app.js, v432): (1) honest 'Synced' — completeMessageSyncUi now also gates on Number(skipped)===0 + Number(incompletePrivateStreamCount)===0 + the reasons private_key_open_failed/partial_stream_pending/index_limit_without_cursor, so the header shows 'delayed'/'message parts pending'/'message key mismatch' instead of a false '✓ Synced'; (2) transient-not-permanent — a transient guard (isTonRpcVerificationSoftReadError || isTonRpcTransientError) sits BEFORE the unreadable branch in scanPrivateEntryId and returns {ok:false} (pins the cursor → re-walk next cycle once RPC recovers) instead of dropping; the 'unavailable' token was removed from isPrivateOpenKeyMismatchError; only deterministic crypto/structural mismatches remain permanently-unreadable (correct, decrypt is hash-verified-before-decrypt so it cannot intermittently fail); (3) multipart surfacing — incompletePrivateStreamCount is now plumbed into privateSyncResult + the gate + privateSyncStatusText ('message parts pending') so a stale incomplete multipart (an image) never reports a clean 'Synced'. REFUTED (not the cause): anonymous-thread mis-filing (those messages are visible in a separate thread), dedup collision (content-addressed), transient-decrypt (hash verified before AES-GCM). Tests: new PWA-DELIVERY-01 (the honest-Synced gate) + updated PWA-CONFIG-07D (transient guard before the unreadable branch + the 'unavailable' token gone). app v431->v432, SW cache v502->v503; deploy-prep regenerated (prod bundle c7c220e9..., productionReady=true). NOTE: v432 fixes delivery FORWARD; already-dropped messages buried below the persisted cursor are recovered only by a one-time full index re-walk (forceIndexRescan, normalizes the cursor to null) on the affected device. PENDING follow-ups (owner-noted): cross-session retry for genuinely-stuck entries (don't bury silently; surface 'undelivered' after a cross-session cap) + double-publish hardening. npm.cmd test = 114/114 test files, 1000/1000 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).

2026-06-15 RPC verifier 429 graceful-degradation fix. After the genesis migration the keyless toncenter verifier (the second of the two dual-provider read transports, ~1 rps) answered 429 under sync load; noteTonRpcTransportFailure only parked verifier-only transports on 401/403, never on 429 (isTonRpcHardTransportError excludes 429), so isVerificationDegraded() stayed false, criticalChainReadOptions kept requesting verification, and every critical read (private index sync, getPrivateEntry confirmation, getAvatar hydration) re-hit the throttled verifier and threw RPC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE -- which spun the publish confirmation-retry loop (re-broadcasts that occasionally hit transient toncenter 500s, since broadcast has no read-fallback). Fix (web/vault-ton-rpc-provider.mjs): a verifier-only transport that answers 429/RATE_LIMITED now parks for the same long window as a 401/403 denial, so verification degrades to the live gateway and reads stop re-hammering the throttled host. Regression test VAULT-RPC-04I8B mirrors the 403 park test with a 429 verifier (parks immediately, isVerificationDegraded true, single verifier probe, unverified reads still flow). vault-ton-rpc-provider.mjs bumped v38->v39 across its 8 importers, service-worker cache v494->v495. npm.cmd test passed locally with 111/111 test files and 986/986 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).
